model_semantics_review.finding: USR_DUMMY independently gates forwarding. CTRL chooses QIO four lanes, DIO two, fast/DOUT/QOUT one. Builtin READ opcode follows CTRL; USR preserves configured opcode. All other zero-initialized transactions retain no dummy by default.

Combined ceil(addr_bits + clocks*lanes)-ceil(addr_bits) is correct for the current byte-oriented SSI contract. SDK QIO28/5 sends four address bytes plus two dummy bytes, total48 bits; SDK DIO28/2 sends four plus zero, total32 bits. Separate phase rounding would add one byte in both cases.

Enabled dummy bytes are transferred while CS stays selected before caller data and their received bytes are discarded. Classic flash selects the existing byte-dummy-cycles contract; shared NOR implementation is unchanged.
Normal full32-bit backing state at DPORT+0xcc resets to documented0xfffce030. SDK RMW can set and clear real bits; no fabricated0x8f8f, assertion removal or Wi-Fi-success shortcut.

pinned_primary_source_support: SDK6.0.2 spi_flash_hal_common.inc:117-132 and239-242 explicitly specify classic ESP32 QIO28/5 and trailing-one address mode bits.
SDK6.0.2 esp32 spi_flash_ll.h:247-275,364-398 defines mode flags, aligned usr address and dummy-cycle encoding/gate.
SDK6.0.2 dport_reg.h:1031-1062 defines full32-bit R/W address/reset and common/Wi-Fi/BT/RNG masks; clk_gate_ll.h:86-151 performs real RMW.

Pinned m25p80.c:1008-1143,1216-1226,1790 defines explicit byte-dummy-cycles fast/DIO/QIO counts and QE-off output. C3 implementation is a comparison, not proof that its bit packing can be copied unchanged.

driver_review.independent_oracles: Compares MMIO data to fresh synthetic backing bytes, with two distinct SPIFFS-sized sentinels and three addresses; lengths2/3/16/64 expose partial-word, skipped-byte and address errors. QE-off/readback and omitted-dummy negatives test protocol sensitivity. DPORT expectations cover reset, zero/all/high-bit writes and enable/disable RMW rather than a fixed required mask.
driver_review.actual_acceptance_requirement: Root must require187 saved check rows, zero false rows, unchanged inputs, no controller errors, actual stdout EOF/reader join and owner cleanup. Driver itself does not separately assert len(checks)==187; immutable current loops yield187.
driver_review.owned_process: Fresh subprocess handle; qtest stdio pipes; no socket listener; both CPUs stopped by qtest accelerator/-S; no firmware, serial, NIC, audio or display. Dedicated output is a fresh direct child of an existing .build directory; no path with comma or newline enters QEMU options.
driver_review.preservation: Fresh synthetic4MiB flash, -snapshot, before/after identity for flash, chosen emulator, driver, two ROMs and six selected model sources. This is selected-source preservation, not full build dependency closure.
driver_review.lifecycle: Per-command three-second response wait, MMIO deadline60 seconds, watchdog errors/queue/read errors fail incomplete; closes only owned process with bounded terminate/kill waits. Requires actual b-empty pipe read, no partial line, reader join, and final size checks. Forced owner termination is recorded, not guest natural shutdown.
driver_review.bounds: Deadline covers MMIO phase; bounded cleanup and input hashing follow. 32MiB logs are checked by a20ms polling watchdog and final reject, so this is a monitored soft cap with overshoot rejection, not an OS-enforced hard quota.

unimplemented_or_unverified_scope: No compiler, QTest, negative baseline, SPI2/SPI3 regression or production guest was executed by this reviewer.
SSI remains byte-oriented; arbitrary partial-bit waveforms, analog latency, every flash manufacturer/mode and complete hardware conformance are not established.
DPORT storage does not implement RF, calibration, association or real networking; CORE_RST_EN behavior is outside this change.
Original firmware/image/config and prior captures remain untouched; existing production startup NONPASS is not reclassified.
Patch application and compilation in a fresh branch/worktree, actual187 MMIO checks, independent unchanged-baseline controls and existing SPI2/SPI3 regressions remain root execution work.
